Identity-scope guard: no infertility or sterility edge is authored - no catalog identity for male infertility exists (female-infertility is out of scope), and the mumps-orchitis fertility literature concerns that viral identity rather than the generic epididymitis-orchitis identity; the fertility pathway is recorded as an evidence gap.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 29 (2026-09-23): one bounded testicular-atrophy association authored from the post-orchitis atrophy literature - Choi 2020's ultrasonographic series documents testicular volume loss of 23-55% (mean 44.7%) occurring 25-230 days after mumps orchitis, and Yapanoglu 2010's semen-and-hormone follow-up documents testicular function loss after orchitis with FSH/LH elevation in the atrophy groups; the mumps-anchored guard (the quantified evidence is mumps-virus scoped; bacterial epididymo-orchitis atrophy is ultrasound-documented but less quantified) and the unilateral-compensation guard (contralateral testis may preserve endocrine function) are recorded.

No abscesses or varicocele-hydrocele edge was authored: the epididymo-orchitis abscess literature is imaging-review class without complication denominators, and reactive hydrocele is an acute-phase finding rather than a catalog-fit chronic outcome; both pathways are recorded here.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Testicular atrophy after orchitis is ultrasonographically documented: Choi 2020's series of eight post-mumps-orchitis patients found atrophic testes 23-55% smaller in volume (mean 44.7% loss) at 25-230 days after the orchitis episode, Yapanoglu 2010's long-term follow-up documents significantly lower sperm density and counts with elevated FSH and LH in the orchitis-atrophy groups, and the imaging literature reviews testicular atrophy as a recognized sequela of severe epididymo-orchitis generally.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the quantified volume-loss evidence is mumps-orchitis scoped while the primary identity is generic (bacterial epididymitis, viral orchitis, and non-infectious inflammations differ in severity and tissue pressure), atrophy must be distinguished from pre-existing volume asymmetry and prior torsion or trauma, and endocrine compensation by the contralateral testis means sonographic atrophy does not equal functional failure in the individual.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized pressure-and-autoimmune-tissue-loss pathway: severe intratesticular inflammation and edema raise intratesticular pressure against the tunica albuginea, compressing seminiferous tubules and the microvasculature; direct viral or bacterial cytopathic injury to germ cells combines with pressure ischemia and, in some cases, secondary autoimmune sensitization to sperm antigens after blood-testis barrier breakdown, producing progressive tubular atrophy and volume loss over weeks to months. Individual attribution requires sonographic documentation with compatible chronology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The atrophy association is quantified mainly in the mumps-orchitis subset and case-series class for the generic identity; sonographic volume loss must be documented bilaterally with serial measurements, pre-existing asymmetry and prior torsion or trauma excluded, and endocrine function assessed separately because sonographic atrophy does not establish hypogonadism; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented epididymitis-orchitis episode (etiology, severity, treatment); testicular volume by ultrasound with serial measurements and compatible chronology; endocrine evaluation (testosterone, FSH, LH) and semen analysis where fertility is at issue; exclusion of pre-existing atrophy, prior torsion, varicocele, and trauma; urology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Pre-existing testicular volume asymmetry or congenital hypoplasia
Klinefelter syndrome or other primary testicular failure

suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: post-orchitis atrophy is ultrasonographically and functionally documented, but the quantified evidence is mumps-scoped and the generic identity's non-viral subsets are case-class; no causation is forced.
